primary_artifact: /Volumes/HMI-Library/heavy-metal-index-raw/Manual Fetch Kimi /June 3 Folder/[AUTO-DE] FAQs about aluminium in food and products intended for consumers.pdf
disposition_reason: BfR consumer FAQ (20 July 2020) on aluminium. Its only cocoa content is one exposure-ranking sentence: cocoa and chocolate products account for 6% of adult dietary Al intake in Germany (4th-ranked food group). It gives no cocoa or chocolate Al concentrations; the only concentrations are generic (processed foods on average <5 mg/kg fresh mass, few foods >20 mg/kg).
disposition_locator: FAQ "Via which foods do adults consume the most aluminium in Germany?" (p.4); "In what quantities is aluminium found in food?" (p.2)

study.material_scope: cocoa and chocolate products (food-group level only)

exposure_context.item: Cocoa and chocolate products share of total dietary Al intake, adults, Germany
exposure_context.note: Other top groups: instant tea drinks 11%, mixed raw vegetable salads 8%, tea drinks 7%, multigrain bread 4%; these five account for 36% of intake. Underlying data refer to the 2019 BfR total-Al intake opinion (not this document).

exposure_context.item: Generic: processed and ready-to-eat foods average <5 mg/kg Al fresh mass; few foods >20 mg/kg

regulatory.instrument: Regulation (EU) No 380/2012 (food additive use of aluminium-containing additives)
regulatory.product: food additives generally; no cocoa-specific limit
